<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I have a clear picture of how CSS and JS are loaded on the page.

Page-specific JavaScript loads on demand. Global CSS loads everywhere. Swiper and GLightbox CSS are always fetched. The lazy CSS path exists but no plugin uses it.

Global JavaScript also loads everywhere. Eager scripts concatenate into script.js. Lazy scripts concatenate into script-lazy.js. search.js and deferred-media.js run on every page. The result is partial on-demand loading.

The `lazy` flag only defers download priority. It does not restrict loading to pages that actually need those assets.
</details></think>

_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

**Partially.** Feature scripts are page-scoped; core CSS and most theme plugins are not.

### What is page-scoped (true on-demand)

Feature JS is included only in the layouts that need it, via `fingerprint-asset`:

| Asset | Where |
|---|---|
| `notes-graph.js`, `wikilink-preview.js`, `notes-flashcard.js`, `notes-copy-md.js` | notes single |
| `notes-list.js`, random helpers | notes list |
| `notes-review.js`, `notes-cards.js`, `randomizer.js`, etc. | their own pages |
| `notes-copy-md.js` | blog single |

Mermaid also loads only when the shortcode runs.

### What loads on every page

From `baseof.html` → `style.html` + cached `script.html`:

**CSS (always)**
- Tailwind main bundle
- Swiper + GLightbox CSS (`lazy = false` in `hugo.toml`)
- Self-hosted fonts

There is a lazy-CSS path (`media="print"` → swap via `deferred-media.js`), but **no CSS plugins currently use `lazy = true`**.

**JS (always)**
- Eager bundle: `touch-controls`, **Swiper**, `toc`, `scroll-progress`, `main.js`
- Lazy bundle (`defer`/`async`, still every page): cookie, GLightbox, gallery-slider, accordion, tab, modal, youtube-lite, back-to-top, share
- Plus: `search.js`, `deferred-media.js`

### Important nuance

`lazy = true` here means “deferred download,” **not** “only if this page uses it.” Swiper CSS/JS still ship site-wide even on pages with no slider.

**Bottom line:** notes/blog feature JS is on-demand; global theme CSS/JS (including Swiper/GLightbox) is not.

_**User**_

some items here are not always needed on the page:

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Several lazy-bundle items are not always needed on every page.

Evaluating minimal loading strategies for each item. Back-to-top may stay global or move to its partial. Share only loads when the social-share partial renders. Cookie consent needs checking to confirm whether its script is conditional.

The remaining lazy items only load when their shortcodes appear. Hugo cannot detect shortcodes at layout time, so moving script tags directly into each shortcode or partial is the cleanest solution. This follows the existing fingerprint-asset pattern already used for notes feature JS.

Vendor shortcodes cannot be edited directly. They should be overridden in the project's `layouts/` directory instead. A footer partial that scans `.Content` for markers is possible but fragile. The better approach is to remove these scripts from the global lazy list and include them only within the partials or shortcodes that actually need them.

Using `.Page.Store` to flag required scripts is blocked by the cached `script.html` partial. Because the script block is globally cached, it cannot read per-page flags set by shortcodes. The fix must either stop caching the script partial or split global scripts from page-specific ones.

Page-specific scripts should load outside the cached partial, either in baseof after the script block, in content layouts, or directly inside the shortcodes that need them. Ponytail will use fingerprint-asset inside those shortcodes and drop them from the global plugins list. Need to check for existing project overrides of vendor shortcodes. Also need to verify whether swiper is only for the gallery or also eager for homepage testimonials, and whether the youtube shortcode duplicates youtube-lite.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The user agreed these items should not load on every page.

Cookie.js will be removed entirely since cookies are disabled. Back-to-top and share scripts will load on demand via partials. Accordion, tab, modal, gallery-slider, glightbox, and youtube-lite will only load when their shortcodes are used.

The cleanest approach avoids editing vendor files. Shortcodes will set Page.Store flags to track loaded scripts. Each script loads only once per page. This prevents duplicate injections.

Swiper CSS and JS must remain eager because gallery pages need them immediately. Swiper JS currently loads eagerly rather than lazily. The plan is to remove the listed scripts from hugo.toml plugins.js. Swiper CSS and JS may also shift to on-demand loading for gallery and slider pages.

Checking whether testimonials use Swiper.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The image shortcode with GLightbox may be used more widely and needs checking too.

A single helper partial using Page.Store could prevent duplicate assets across the site. Touch-controls for Swiper are also being considered.

CSS for Swiper and GLightbox will move out of the main concat and load as separate link tags on demand. Thin shortcode wrappers will be created in layouts/shortcodes, since Hugo prefers those over module layouts.

Duplicating vendor shortcode markup inside custom wrappers is undesirable. Calling the original module shortcode from a wrapper is difficult because names conflict. A Store-based footer approach avoids overriding shortcode bodies entirely. Render hooks were dismissed.

A regex scan of `.RawContent` in a baseof footer partial could detect shortcode usage without overriding individual shortcodes. This risks missing nested includes, draft versus published states, and other format variations.

The image shortcode with a GLightbox class does not actually use the gallery shortcode. A regex scan of raw content is too fragile. Copying vendor HTML into custom shortcode overrides is a better path, since the affected components are small. Gallery and slider will also need swiper and glightbox assets loaded on demand. Cookie.js can be removed entirely if cookies are disabled.

youtube-lite.js is unused on most pages because content relies on the standard `youtube` shortcode with iframe embeds. It can be removed from the global bundle and loaded only from its own shortcode override. The cookie-consent partial already contains an inline script that depends on the Cookies global, so cookie.js would be required if consent is enabled later. Modal usage in content still needs verification.
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Implementing on-demand loading for the optional lazy bundle items.

A `need-asset.html` helper will emit each asset once per page via Store. Shortcodes will set need flags and load assets directly. Vendor shortcodes will be overridden with thin project files that include the original markup.

A simpler approach uses a non-cached partial that scans `.RawContent` for shortcode patterns. This detects whether accordion, gallery, slider, or zoomable image shortcodes appear on the page. It then conditionally loads the corresponding assets. This avoids fragile shortcode overrides.

The image shortcode is vendor-built and cannot be injected without an override. RawContent scanning is fragile but acceptable for this site’s limited shortcode use. It misses shortcodes inside partials and commented-out ones. Share scripts will load in `social-share.html`.

Cookie will be removed entirely. Back-to-top will load in its own partial. A single `page-shortcode-assets.html` partial will handle the remaining lazy assets via Store flags set by thin shortcode wrappers. The wrappers may reuse the original vendor templates without duplicating HTML.

Hugo 0.120+ prevents calling a shortcode by its own name. The wrapper will load the script once via Store, then render the original vendor template body directly.

Copying vendor shortcode bodies into the project would create maintenance debt. A single `conditional-plugins.html` partial in `baseof` is preferable. It scans `.RawContent` for shortcode patterns and loads assets once per page. Deferred scripts can safely sit at the end of the body. Glightbox and swiper CSS remain in the head.

Loading CSS at the end of the body risks a flash of unstyled content on gallery pages. That is acceptable for rare pages.

The raw-content scanner places script tags at the end of the body after the main script. This keeps deferred scripts safe.

Zoomable images need GLightbox without the gallery-slider script. Gallery-slider.js always initializes GLightbox. It also initializes Swiper. The two are tightly coupled.

Gallery-slider.js only initializes Swiper when a `.gallery-slider` element exists. Zoomable image pages therefore need only glightbox and gallery-slider assets, while slider pages additionally require swiper. The uncached `conditional-plugins.html` partial will be invoked from `baseof` after `script.html`.

Swiper and GLightbox CSS will also leave the global stylesheet and load conditionally. Touch-controls, TOC, and scroll-progress remain eager and global. The concrete plan is to create `layouts/_partials/essentials/conditional-plugins.html`, invoke it from `layouts/baseof.html`, strip the listed lazy bundle items from `hugo.toml`, and wire `share.js` into `social-share.html`.

Project-level `layouts/_partials/components/` files will override the theme’s social-share and back-to-top partials. The cookie script will be removed entirely because cookies are disabled.

Checking module mounts to confirm the correct asset path for the accordion script.
</details></think>

Yes — for the shortcode plugins, it scans the page’s raw markdown (`.RawContent`) for patterns like `{{< accordion`, `{{< tabs`, `{{< gallery`, `zoomable="true"`, etc., then emits the matching CSS/JS.

It’s a text match, not Hugo’s shortcode registry. So it can miss shortcodes that only appear via a partial (none today), and it can false-positive on commented-out shortcode text that still looks like `{{< …`.

`share.js` and `back-to-top.js` are different: they load from the partial that renders that UI, not from the shortcode scan.
